source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֨א הַגּוֹרָ֜ל לִבְנֵ֤י יוֹסֵף֙ מִיַּרְדֵּ֣ן יְרִיח֔וֹ לְמֵ֥י יְרִיח֖וֹ מִזְרָ֑חָה הַמִּדְבָּ֗ר עֹלֶ֧ה מִירִיח֛וֹ בָּהָ֖ר בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out the lot for [the] sons of Joseph from [the] Jordan [of] Jericho to [the] waters of Jericho eastward, the wilderness going up from Jericho in the hill country [to] Bethel.

en.L: And the lot for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Joseph went out from the Jordan at Jericho, to the waters of Jericho on the east, the wilderness going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
en.B: The allotment for the descendants of Joseph ran from the Jordan at Jericho, east of the springs of Jericho, through the wilderness that climbs from Jericho up into the hill country to Bethel.
en.R: Joseph's descendants were given their land by lot. Its southern border started at the Jordan River near Jericho, east of the springs there. From Jericho it climbed through the desert into the hill country and on to Bethel.

sw.L: Na kura ya wana wa Yusufu ilitoka kutoka Yordani karibu na Yeriko, hadi maji ya Yeriko upande wa mashariki, nyika inayopanda kutoka Yeriko kupitia nchi ya milima hadi Betheli.
sw.B: Nchi waliyogawiwa wazao wa Yusufu ilianzia Yordani karibu na Yeriko, mashariki ya chemchemi za Yeriko, ikapita katika nyika inayopanda kutoka Yeriko kuingia nchi ya milima hadi Betheli.
sw.R: Wazao wa Yusufu walipewa nchi yao kwa kura. Mpaka wake wa kusini ulianzia Mto Yordani karibu na Yeriko, mashariki ya chemchemi za huko. Kutoka Yeriko ulipanda kupitia jangwa kuingia nchi ya milima, ukaendelea hadi Betheli.

decisions.choice: the lot went out: the land fell to them by lot
decisions.reason: Casting lots was the way the land was shared out, so that the choice was left to God (14:2; Numbers 26:55-56; Proverbs 16:33). "The lot went out" means the lot was drawn for them, and the word "lot" then stands for the land it gave: the description that follows is the line of that land.

decisions.choice: the sons of Joseph: the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh together
decisions.reason: Joseph's two sons each became a tribe (verse 4; Genesis 48:5). Here they receive one lot together, and the line traced in verses 1-3 is the southern edge of their whole share. Chapter 16 then gives Ephraim's part (verses 5-10) and chapter 17 Manasseh's.

decisions.choice: the waters of Jericho: the springs at Jericho
decisions.reason: Jericho was an oasis watered by strong springs (2 Kings 2:19-22). The border starts at the Jordan, east of these springs, and runs west. The same line is the northern border of Benjamin (18:12-13).

decisions.choice: the wilderness going up: kept as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: and it went up from Jericho into the wilderness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence is compressed: "the wilderness" stands without a linking word, describing the dry, rising country the border crosses between Jericho and Bethel (compare 18:12, "the wilderness of Beth-aven"). The ancient Greek translation reads it differently, joining the words to the line of the border. The Hebrew is followed. This note is from general knowledge of the Greek and should be checked by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: allotment
decisions.reason: Balanced says "allotment" for the share given by lot, since "the lot ran from" would be unclear (m1). Literal keeps "lot"; Readable says they "were given their land by lot".

decisions.choice: Its southern border
decisions.reason: Readable names this as the southern border, which is what verses 1-3 trace (m2), and breaks the sentence into short ones.

source.text: וְיָצָ֥א מִבֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל ל֑וּזָה וְעָבַ֛ר אֶל־גְּב֥וּל הָאַרְכִּ֖י עֲטָרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And goes out from Bethel to Luz and passes on to [the] territory of the Archite[s] [at] Ataroth.

en.L: And it goes out from Bethel to Luz, and passes along to the territory of the Archites, [to] Ataroth.
en.B: From Bethel it goes on to Luz and passes along to Ataroth, in the territory of the Archites.
en.R: From Bethel it went on to Luz, and then along to the town of Ataroth, where the Archite clan lived.

sw.L: Na unatoka Betheli hadi Luzu, na kupita hadi eneo la Waarki, [hadi] Atarothi.
sw.B: Kutoka Betheli unaendelea hadi Luzu na kupita hadi Atarothi, katika eneo la Waarki.
sw.R: Kutoka Betheli ulienda hadi Luzu, kisha ukaendelea hadi mji wa Atarothi, walikoishi ukoo wa Waarki.

decisions.choice: goes out ... passes: the course of the border, not events in time
decisions.reason: From here on the verbs describe the path the boundary line takes, as one would trace it on a map: it goes out, passes, goes down, ends. The Hebrew form used here, common in boundary lists (15:2-11; 18:12-20), describes a standing fact rather than something that happened once.

decisions.choice: from Bethel to Luz: two neighboring places
alternatives: Luz as another name for Bethel
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Luz is named as the older name of Bethel (Genesis 28:19; Joshua 18:13; Judges 1:23). Here the two are distinct points on the line, probably because the town of Luz and the shrine of Bethel stood a short distance apart; 18:13 also speaks of the line passing "toward Luz, to the side of Luz, that is Bethel".

decisions.choice: the Archites: a clan living near Ataroth
decisions.reason: The Archites are known from David's friend Hushai the Archite (2 Samuel 15:32). Their land lay on this border, near the town of Ataroth, which is probably the Ataroth-addar of verse 5 and 18:13.

decisions.choice: the town of Ataroth, where the Archite clan lived
alternatives: the territory of the Archites at Ataroth
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" and "clan" so the reader can tell the place from the people (terms doc for Joshua's town lists).

decisions.choice: went ... went along
decisions.reason: Readable tells the line in the past tense, as a story of where the border ran, which reads more easily for new readers. Literal and Balanced keep the present that describes a border (m1).

source.text: וְיָֽרַד־יָ֜מָּה אֶל־גְּב֣וּל הַיַּפְלֵטִ֗י עַ֣ד גְּב֧וּל בֵּית־חוֹרֹ֛ן תַּחְתּ֖וֹן וְעַד־גָּ֑זֶר וְהָי֥וּ תֹצְאֹתָ֖יו יָֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And goes down westward to [the] territory of the Japhletite[s] as far as [the] territory of Beth-horon lower and as far as Gezer, and are its goings out to the sea.

en.L: And it goes down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Gezer, and its end is at the sea.
en.B: Then it goes down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon, and on to Gezer, and it ends at the sea.
en.R: Then it went down west to the land of the Japhletite clan, as far as Lower Beth-horon and on to Gezer. It ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

sw.L: Na unashuka kuelekea magharibi hadi eneo la Wayafleti, hadi eneo la Beth-horoni ya Chini na hadi Gezeri, na mwisho wake ni baharini.
sw.B: Kisha unashuka kuelekea magharibi hadi eneo la Wayafleti, hadi eneo la Beth-horoni ya Chini, na kuendelea hadi Gezeri, nao unaishia baharini.
sw.R: Kisha ulishuka kuelekea magharibi hadi nchi ya ukoo wa Wayafleti, hadi Beth-horoni ya Chini, ukaendelea hadi Gezeri. Uliishia Bahari ya Mediterania.

decisions.choice: the Japhletites: a clan of the region
decisions.reason: The Japhletites are not mentioned anywhere else in the Old Testament. A man named Japhlet appears in the line of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:32-33), but the link is not certain. They were a group living on the border between Bethel and Beth-horon.

decisions.choice: Lower Beth-horon and Gezer: the descent to the coastal plain
decisions.reason: Upper and Lower Beth-horon stood at the top and the foot of the steep pass that leads down from the hill country to the lowland (10:10-11). Gezer lay beyond, at the edge of the plain, guarding the road to the coast.

decisions.choice: its goings out are at the sea: it ends at the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: "Goings out" is the regular word in the boundary lists for the point where a line runs out (15:4, 11). "The sea" on the west is the Mediterranean.

decisions.choice: its end is (L); ends (B); ended (R)
alternatives: its goings out are at the sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that the line ends at the sea (m3). Literal says "its end is at the sea", as in Numbers 34:5 and through these lists.

decisions.choice: the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: Readable gives the modern name of the sea (m3), as in 1:4.

records.literal_gloss: And received inheritance [the] sons of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
en.B: So the descendants of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
en.R: This is how Joseph's descendants, the tribes of Manasseh and Ephraim, received their land.

sw.L: Na wana wa Yusufu, Manase na Efraimu, wakapokea urithi wao.
sw.B: Hivyo wazao wa Yusufu, Manase na Efraimu, walipokea urithi wao.
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo wazao wa Yusufu, yaani makabila ya Manase na Efraimu, walivyopokea nchi yao.

decisions.choice: received their inheritance: took possession of land as a lasting family holding
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive or take as an inheritance. The land given by lot was to stay with each tribe and its families for good, passed down from one generation to the next (Numbers 27:8-11; 36:7-9).

decisions.choice: Manasseh and Ephraim: the older son named first
decisions.reason: Manasseh was Joseph's firstborn, and he is named first here, as in Genesis 48:1. Yet Jacob set Ephraim ahead of him (Genesis 48:14-20), and Ephraim's share is described first in the verses that follow.

decisions.choice: the tribes of Manasseh and Ephraim; their land
alternatives: Manasseh and Ephraim received their inheritance
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the two names are tribes, and says "land" for the inheritance (m1).

source.text: וַיְהִ֛י גְּב֥וּל בְּנֵֽי־אֶפְרַ֖יִם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֑ם וַיְהִ֞י גְּב֤וּל נַחֲלָתָם֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה עַטְר֣וֹת אַדָּ֔ר עַד־בֵּ֥ית חוֹרֹ֖ן עֶלְיֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And was [the] territory of [the] sons of Ephraim by their clans; and was [the] border of their inheritance eastward Ataroth-addar as far as Beth-horon upper.

en.L: And the territory of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ephraim by their clans was [this]: the border of their inheritance on the east was Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon.
en.B: This was the territory of the Ephraimites, clan by clan. The border of their inheritance ran on the east from Ataroth-addar to Upper Beth-horon,
en.R: Here is the land of the tribe of Ephraim, family by family. The border of their land started on the east at Ataroth-addar and ran to Upper Beth-horon.

sw.L: Na eneo la wana wa Efraimu kufuatana na koo zao [lilikuwa hili]: mpaka wa urithi wao upande wa mashariki ulikuwa Atarothi-adari hadi Beth-horoni ya Juu.
sw.B: Hili ndilo lililokuwa eneo la Waefraimu, ukoo kwa ukoo. Mpaka wa urithi wao upande wa mashariki ulianzia Atarothi-adari hadi Beth-horoni ya Juu,
sw.R: Hii ndiyo nchi ya kabila la Efraimu, jamaa kwa jamaa. Mpaka wa nchi yao ulianzia upande wa mashariki huko Atarothi-adari, ukaenda hadi Beth-horoni ya Juu.

decisions.choice: on the east, Ataroth-addar to Upper Beth-horon: the southern line seen from its east end
decisions.reason: This is the same southern border as verses 1-3, given more briefly, from Ataroth-addar on its eastern part to Upper Beth-horon on the west (compare 18:13). "On the east" marks where the description begins.

decisions.choice: Ataroth-addar: a border town
decisions.reason: Ataroth-addar is probably the Ataroth of verse 2, named more fully. It stood on the line between Ephraim and Benjamin (18:13). It is a different place from the Ataroth of verse 7, on the eastern side.

decisions.choice: the Ephraimites
decisions.reason: Balanced says "the Ephraimites" for "the sons of Ephraim", a word that already includes the whole tribe, as "Israelites" does for "the sons of Israel" (terms doc). Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: ran ... to Upper Beth-horon, (comma)
decisions.reason: Balanced ends the record with a comma and runs into verse 6, which continues the same description of the border.

source.text: וְיָצָ֨א הַגְּב֜וּל הַיָּ֗מָּה הַֽמִּכְמְתָת֙ מִצָּפ֔וֹן וְנָסַ֧ב הַגְּב֛וּל מִזְרָ֖חָה תַּאֲנַ֣ת שִׁלֹ֑ה וְעָבַ֣ר אוֹת֔וֹ מִמִּזְרַ֖ח יָנֽוֹחָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And goes out the border to the sea; the Michmethath on [the] north; and turns the border eastward [to] Taanath-shiloh and passes it on [the] east [to] Janoah.

en.L: And the border goes out toward the sea, the Michmethath being on the north, and the border turns eastward to Taanath-shiloh and passes by it on the east to Janoah.
en.B: and out to the sea. From Michmethath on the north the border turns east toward Taanath-shiloh and passes by it on the east to Janoah.
en.R: From there the border went west to the sea. On the north side, it started at Michmethath, turned east toward Taanath-shiloh, and passed east of it to Janoah.

sw.L: Na mpaka unatokea kuelekea baharini, Mikmethathi ikiwa upande wa kaskazini; na mpaka unageuka kuelekea mashariki hadi Taanath-shilo na kuupita upande wa mashariki hadi Yanoa.
sw.B: na kutokea baharini. Kutoka Mikmethathi upande wa kaskazini mpaka unageuka kuelekea mashariki hadi Taanath-shilo, na kuupita upande wa mashariki hadi Yanoa.
sw.R: Kutoka hapo mpaka ulienda magharibi hadi baharini. Upande wa kaskazini ulianzia Mikmethathi, ukageuka kuelekea mashariki hadi Taanath-shilo, ukaupita upande wa mashariki hadi Yanoa.

decisions.choice: goes out to the sea; Michmethath on the north: two parts of the line meeting at Michmethath
alternatives: the border goes from Michmethath on the north to the sea
decisions.reason: The verse is hard to follow. It seems to finish the southern line westward "to the sea", and then to start the northern border at Michmethath, a point near Shechem (17:7), tracing it first eastward (verses 6-7) and then westward from Tappuah (verse 8). Another way to read it is that the line goes west to the sea from Michmethath itself. Either way, Michmethath is a point on Ephraim's northern border.

decisions.choice: Taanath-shiloh and Janoah: towns east and south-east of Shechem
decisions.reason: Taanath-shiloh lay east of Shechem; it is a different place from Shiloh, where the tabernacle was set up (18:1). Janoah lay further to the south-east, on the way down toward the Jordan valley.

decisions.choice: and out to the sea.
decisions.reason: Balanced finishes the sentence begun in verse 5 here, then starts a new sentence for the northern line (m1).

decisions.choice: On the north side, it started at Michmethath
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that a second part of the border starts here (m1). Since the reading is not certain, this is marked for reviewers.

source.text: וְיָרַ֥ד מִיָּנ֖וֹחָה עֲטָר֣וֹת וְנַעֲרָ֑תָה וּפָגַע֙ בִּֽירִיח֔וֹ וְיָצָ֖א הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And goes down from Janoah [to] Ataroth and to Naarah, and touches on Jericho and goes out [at] the Jordan.

en.L: And it goes down from Janoah to Ataroth and to Naarah, and touches Jericho, and goes out at the Jordan.
en.B: From Janoah it goes down to Ataroth and Naarah, reaches Jericho, and comes out at the Jordan.
en.R: From Janoah it went down to Ataroth and Naarah, reached Jericho, and ended at the Jordan River.

sw.L: Na unashuka kutoka Yanoa hadi Atarothi na hadi Naara, na kugusa Yeriko, na kutokea Yordani.
sw.B: Kutoka Yanoa unashuka hadi Atarothi na Naara, unafika Yeriko, na kutokea Yordani.
sw.R: Kutoka Yanoa ulishuka hadi Atarothi na Naara, ukafika Yeriko, ukaishia Mto Yordani.

decisions.choice: Ataroth and Naarah: places on the descent to the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: This Ataroth is in the east, below Janoah, and is not the Ataroth of verse 2. Naarah is probably the Naaran of 1 Chronicles 7:28, a town of Ephraim north of Jericho.

decisions.choice: touches Jericho: reaches the area of Jericho
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet or touch. The line comes down to the region of Jericho, which itself belonged to Benjamin (18:21), and then reaches the Jordan. So the eastern end of Ephraim's land is closed off near where the southern line began (verse 1).

decisions.choice: reaches
decisions.reason: "Touches" is kept at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "reaches", which is how a border is described in English.

source.text: מִתַּפּ֜וּחַ יֵלֵ֨ךְ הַגְּב֥וּל יָ֨מָּה֙ נַ֣חַל קָנָ֔ה וְהָי֥וּ תֹצְאֹתָ֖יו הַיָּ֑מָּה זֹ֗את נַחֲלַ֛ת מַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵי־אֶפְרַ֖יִם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: From Tappuah goes the border westward [the] wadi [of] Kanah, and are its goings out to the sea. This [is the] inheritance of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Ephraim by their clans,

en.L: From Tappuah the border goes westward [to] the wadi of Kanah, and its end is at the sea. This [is] the inheritance of the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ephraim by their clans,
en.B: From Tappuah the border goes west along the Wadi Kanah and ends at the sea. This is the inheritance of the Ephraimite tribe, clan by clan,
en.R: On the west side, the border went from Tappuah along the Wadi Kanah, a stream that is dry most of the year, and ended at the sea. This was the land given to the tribe of Ephraim, family by family.

sw.L: Kutoka Tapua mpaka unaenda kuelekea magharibi [hadi] korongo la Kana, na mwisho wake ni baharini. Huu [ndio] urithi wa kabila la wana wa Efraimu kufuatana na koo zao,
sw.B: Kutoka Tapua mpaka unaenda magharibi kando ya Bonde la Kana na kuishia baharini. Huu ndio urithi wa kabila la Efraimu, ukoo kwa ukoo,
sw.R: Upande wa magharibi, mpaka ulienda kutoka Tapua kando ya Bonde la Kana, mkondo ambao huwa mkavu karibu mwaka mzima, ukaishia baharini. Hii ndiyo nchi iliyopewa kabila la Efraimu, jamaa kwa jamaa.

decisions.choice: Tappuah and the wadi of Kanah: the western half of the northern border
decisions.reason: Having traced the northern line eastward from Michmethath (verses 6-7), the text now traces it westward. Tappuah lay on the border with Manasseh (17:7-8). A wadi is a stream bed that is dry most of the year and fills in the rainy season; the Kanah runs west toward the coast and also marks the line between Ephraim and Manasseh in 17:9.

decisions.choice: This is the inheritance ... (continued in verse 9)
alternatives: a full stop at the end of verse 8
decisions.reason: The summary may close the description, or may run on into verse 9: "... by their clans, together with the cities set apart". Literal and Balanced end with a comma to leave that link open.

decisions.choice: wadi of Kanah (L); the Wadi Kanah (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "wadi"; Balanced and Readable use it as part of the name, as with the Wadi of Egypt (15:4), and Readable explains it (m1). The same wording is used in 17:9.

decisions.choice: On the west side
decisions.reason: Readable tells the reader that the description has moved to the western part of the northern border (m1).

source.text: וְהֶעָרִ֗ים הַמִּבְדָּלוֹת֙ לִבְנֵ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם בְּת֖וֹךְ נַחֲלַ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה כָּֽל־הֶעָרִ֖ים וְחַצְרֵיהֶֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: and the cities the set apart for [the] sons of Ephraim in [the] midst of [the] inheritance of [the] sons of Manasseh, all the cities and their villages.

en.L: and the cities set apart for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ephraim [were] in the midst of the inheritance of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Manasseh, all the cities and their villages.
en.B: together with the towns set apart for the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites, all those towns and their villages.
en.R: The people of Ephraim were also given some towns inside the land of Manasseh, with all the villages around them.

sw.L: na miji iliyotengwa kwa ajili ya wana wa Efraimu [ilikuwa] katikati ya urithi wa wana wa Manase, miji yote na vijiji vyake.
sw.B: pamoja na miji iliyotengwa kwa ajili ya Waefraimu ndani ya urithi wa Wamanase, miji hiyo yote na vijiji vyake.
sw.R: Watu wa Efraimu walipewa pia miji kadhaa ndani ya nchi ya Manase, pamoja na vijiji vyote vilivyoizunguka.

decisions.choice: the cities set apart: towns reserved for Ephraim
decisions.reason: The word describes something separated or set aside. These towns stood inside Manasseh's land but were reserved for Ephraim. Chapter 17 shows the same kind of arrangement: the town of Tappuah belonged to Ephraim while the land around it belonged to Manasseh (17:8-9).

decisions.choice: and the cities ...: a phrase continuing verse 8
alternatives: a separate statement: the cities were in Manasseh's inheritance
decisions.reason: The verse has no main verb of its own. It adds the reserved towns to Ephraim's inheritance just summed up in verse 8.

decisions.choice: their villages: the unwalled settlements belonging to each town
decisions.reason: A walled town had smaller open settlements around it that depended on it and were counted with it, as in the lists of chapter 15.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "towns" for places of this size, as in the other town lists of Joshua; Literal keeps "cities".

decisions.choice: the Manassites
decisions.reason: As "the Ephraimites" in verse 5, Balanced uses the tribal name for "the sons of Manasseh".

source.text: וְלֹ֣א הוֹרִ֔ישׁוּ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י הַיּוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּגָ֑זֶר וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֜י בְּקֶ֤רֶב אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד־הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְהִ֖י לְמַס־עֹבֵֽד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And not they dispossessed the Canaanite[s] dwelling in Gezer; and dwelt the Canaanite[s] in [the] midst of Ephraim until the day the this, and became forced labor working.

en.L: But they did not dispossess the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, and the Canaanites have lived in the midst of Ephraim to this day, and they became forced labor, working.
en.B: But they did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, and so Canaanites have lived among the Ephraimites to this day, though they were made to work as forced laborers.
en.R: But the people of Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in the town of Gezer. Those Canaanites still live among them today, but they have to do hard work for Ephraim.

sw.L: Lakini hawakuwafukuza Wakanaani waliokaa Gezeri, na Wakanaani wamekaa katikati ya Efraimu hadi siku hii ya leo, nao wakawa watu wa kazi ya kulazimishwa, wakifanya kazi.
sw.B: Lakini hawakuwafukuza Wakanaani walioishi Gezeri, na kwa hiyo Wakanaani wameishi kati ya Waefraimu mpaka leo, ingawa walilazimishwa kufanya kazi za kutumikishwa.
sw.R: Lakini watu wa Efraimu hawakuwafukuza Wakanaani walioishi katika mji wa Gezeri. Wakanaani hao bado wanaishi kati yao hata leo, lakini wanalazimika kufanya kazi ngumu kwa ajili ya Efraimu.

decisions.choice: did not dispossess: did not drive out
decisions.reason: The verb, used for nations, means to drive them out so as to take their land. God had commanded that the Canaanites be driven out (Numbers 33:52-53; Deuteronomy 7:1-2). The note that Ephraim failed to do so at Gezer is repeated in Judges 1:29, and similar notes follow for Manasseh (17:12-13) and Judah (15:63).

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time the book was written
decisions.reason: The phrase looks from the writer's own day, when Canaanites still lived at Gezer. Later Gezer was captured by a king of Egypt and given to Solomon as a dowry (1 Kings 9:16).

decisions.choice: forced labor, working: a labor force made to serve
decisions.reason: The word means a body of people required to work for others, and "working" stresses that it was hard labor service. The same was done to the Canaanites in other places (17:13; Judges 1:28-35), and Solomon later made such people serve him (1 Kings 9:20-21).

decisions.choice: no additional words: the Hebrew text followed
alternatives: include the Greek addition about Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation adds a sentence saying that Pharaoh king of Egypt went up, captured Gezer and burned it, which agrees with 1 Kings 9:16. The Hebrew text is followed. This note is from general knowledge of the Greek and should be checked by a reviewer.

decisions.choice: drive out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "drive out" for nations (terms doc for this verb); Literal keeps "dispossess".

decisions.choice: the people of Ephraim; the town of
decisions.reason: Readable names who failed to drive the Canaanites out, and adds "the town of" before Gezer.
